title: Adaptive Admission Controller for SLO-aware Preemptive Load Shedding
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Background: We observe short-lived autoscaler thrashing and multi-region failover amplification when unhealthy instances report transient probe failures. Current approaches (hard readiness flips + circuit breakers) either let a flood of requests overload healthy regions during failover or conservatively block traffic causing SLO misses for latency-sensitive customers.

Goal: Implement an adaptive admission controller that gates incoming requests at the front of the serving tier based on a compact SLO-aware budget. The controller should preemptively shed or delay low-priority requests during degradations to preserve latency and error-rate SLOs for high-priority traffic and reduce autoscaler oscillation across regions.

Scope: Front-door admission logic + server-side token buckets, region-aware weighting, fast path for pinned customers, metrics/export hooks, and a canary rollout. Not in scope: full policy UI in Console (will be a follow-up), changes to billing or quota enforcement beyond labels.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Controller exposes per-route admission decision metric and publishes admit_rate, shed_rate, and queued_latency.
2) Under simulated 25% instance degradation in primary region, 95th percentile latency for P0 routes remains within 10% of baseline while total shed_rate for P2 routes increases.
3) Autoscaler oscillation (scale-up/scale-down frequency) reduces by >=30% in fault-injection tests compared to baseline.
4) Canary deployed across 5% of traffic in primary region with automatic rollback if shed_rate for P0 routes > 1% for 10m.
5) Unit/integration tests for admission logic and region-weighting added to CI.
tasks: Design admission token model and region weighting (tech doc)
Implement lightweight admission middleware in serving runtime (C++ hot path)
Add metric instrumentation: admit_rate, shed_rate, queue_time, decision_reasons
Create e2e fault-injection harness that simulates probe flapping and regional capacity loss
Build canary rollout job with automatic traffic steering and rollback on SLO regression
Run load test matrix (latency/throughput/error) and capture baseline vs experimental
Document config knobs and safe defaults in the operations runbook
design_summary:
We will use a two-tier admission model: (1) a global SLO budget coordinator that maintains a short-lived moving window of 'acceptable work' per customer/route and (2) a local admission token bucket per serving process with region-aware weights. The global coordinator emits compact budget signals via the control plane to each region. Local buckets prefer P0/P1 traffic and apply probabilistic shedding for P2/P3 based on current budget. To avoid thundering herd during failover, newly inflight requests are delayed briefly (<=50ms) and re-evaluated rather than immediately rejected when budget is marginal. This smoothing reduces spiky load that triggers autoscaler churn.

Trade-offs: Extra network control plane chatter vs improved centralized budget coordination. Slight added latency for delayed low-priority requests (configurable). Complexity in tuning weights for multi-tenant fairness.

Open questions: How to map existing rate-limiter labels to priority levels for customers with no explicit tier? Should we use conservative defaults or attempt to infer priority from historical token consumption?
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): 5% traffic in primary region for non-critical customers, 1 day observation. Metric gates: P0 shed_rate < 0.5%, P0 p95 latency within 10% baseline.
Phase 2 (regional expand): 25% traffic across primary+secondary with simulated instance failures, 3 day observation.
Phase 3 (global): enable multi-region weighting and fast-failover smoothing for all non-enterprise tenants, 1 week monitoring, then enterprise opt-in.
Rollback: immediate disable flag flips local buckets to permissive admit behaviour, and traffic is rebalanced by smart router.
Monitoring: dashboards for admit_rate/shed_rate by route, per-region autoscaler activity, and SLO regressions tied to evaluation prompt sets.
qa_plan: Unit tests for admission decisions under synthetic budgets. Integration tests running local buckets + mock coordinator. Chaos tests: probe flapping and graceful node termination. Load tests at 0.5x, 1x, 2x baseline QPS with and without admission enabled. Canary triggers automated SLO checks using the existing SLO evaluator; any regression auto-creates an incident runbook alert.
testing_notes: Initial sim harness shows a 38% reduction in autoscaler event rate during a synthetic regional outage when low-priority requests are probabilistically shed. Observed small increase (~20ms) in median latency for P2 routes when admission is active. We'll tune token refill rates and delay windows in Phase 2. Tests reproducible via infra/playbooks/admission-sim in the repo.
